extracted.intended_audience: attorneys/practitioners authorized to practice before the USPTO; Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff; disciplinary counsel
extracted.subtask_description: A final USPTO disciplinary order imposing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 after a state court suspension, describing procedural steps (notice, opportunity to respond), the imposed sanction, publication and notice obligations, and citation to governing statutes and rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, the USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline identical to discipline imposed by a state authority (here, the Supreme Court of the State of Nevada suspended Respondent for 35 days). The OED Director filed a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline requesting imposition of identical discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order initiating reciprocal discipline must be sent (here by certified mail) and must inform the respondent of the request to impose identical discipline; the respondent is given an opportunity to oppose under the grounds listed in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond within forty (40) days under the Notice and Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order provided Respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the state, based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely filing of a response within the 40-day period is the procedural mechanism for the respondent to raise any permissible defenses under § 11.24(d)(1). The Notice here was delivered on January 19, 2018; Respondent did not file a response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond: no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: In light of Respondent's failure to file a response, it is hereby determined that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to respond to the Notice and Order can result in the USPTO treating the matter as unopposed and concluding there is no genuine issue of material fact, permitting imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to the state-imposed sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposition and scope of suspension from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended for thirty-five (35) days from the practice of trademark and other non-patent law before the United States Patent and Trademark Office for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifies the duration (35 days) and the scope (trademark and other non-patent matters). The Order also notes 'Mr. Callister is not authorized to practice before the Office in patent matters,' clarifying the respondent's current patent-practice status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirement in the Official Gazette (Notice of Suspension)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette containing the respondent's name, location, authorization to practice, nature and duration of the suspension, the regulatory citation (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)), and that the action is predicated on a state suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice included a factual summary (e.g., offering $7,000 to a witness, threatening the witness), citations to the violated rules (RPC 3.4(b) and RPC 8.4(d)), and a reference to the OED FOIA Reading Room for disciplinary decisions (http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public under 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted to practice, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement compels communication of the USPTO disciplinary action to relevant state agencies and courts, ensuring reciprocal awareness across jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent must comply with duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires compliance with the specified duties (e.g., duties incident to suspension or disbarment such as notifying clients, returning papers, and other obligations set out in § 11.58). The Order does not restate § 11.58, but mandates adherence to it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory/regulatory authority for discipline: 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites federal statute and USPTO regulations as the legal bases authorizing imposition of reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-court findings of misconduct (factual basis for discipline)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supreme Court of the State of Nevada suspended Jonathan Callister for offering $7,000.00 to a third-party fact witness, if the witness would testify that the will he had witnessed was a fake, and for threatening the witness with civil litigation and criminal exposure if the witness would not testify as Mr. Callister wanted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice reproduces the factual findings that supported the state suspension; these facts are the predicate for the USPTO's reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of Nevada RPC 3.4(b) (offer of inducement to a witness)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supreme Court found that Mr. Callister violated RPC 3.4(b) (fairness to opposing party and counsel: offer of an inducement to a witness that is prohibited by law).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The state-rule violation is treated as the underlying professional misconduct warranting reciprocal discipline under USPTO procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of Nevada RPC 8.4(d) (misconduct prejudicial to the administration of justice)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supreme Court found that Mr. Callister violated RPC 8.4(d) (misconduct prejudicial to the administration of justice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This misconduct finding, together with the RPC 3.4(b) violation, forms the basis for the state suspension and the USPTO's reciprocal action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of Notice by certified mail and proof of delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: On January 10, 2018 a 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' was sent by certified mail (receipt no. 70160910000045132865) notifying Respondent; the Notice and Order was delivered to Respondent on January 19, 2018.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper service (e.g., by certified mail with proof of delivery) is part of the procedural record supporting the USPTO's authority to proceed; documented delivery and the running of the response period are critical to the reciprocal discipline process.
